evidence.detail: rs/C constructs exactly one rs/m/a as protected field hR. Bundled exact-v308 regression tools reflect this field under the descriptive name mouseInputQueue and exercise it through prepareMouseInput/processQueuedMouseInput.

The class owns a fixed 256-entry ring of rs/m/a$a records, synchronized enqueue/drain/reset operations, head/count state and an overflow counter. On overflow it clears and inserts a type-4 reset/sentinel event.
The client shell queues press/move/release records with coordinates and MouseEvent timestamps. Consecutive type-3 motion records are coalesced while preserving min/max x/y excursion bounds.

Bundled QueuedSwitchingRegression proves F-key/tab switching is enqueued into the same ordering domain so it cannot overtake earlier mouse press/move/release events. This is why the name remains QueuedInputBuffer rather than MouseEventQueue.
Client drains the buffer into preallocated rs/m/a$a records in processQueuedMouseInput, dispatching reset, switch/control, press, release and coalesced movement records in FIFO order.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the synchronized client-input ordering buffer. Mouse input is the dominant payload, but exact regressions prove non-mouse switch/control records share the queue.

evidence.detail: The nested record stores event type, secondary code/button, x/y, min/max x/y excursion bounds and one timestamp. Its initializer seeds all movement bounds from the supplied coordinates.

QueuedInputBuffer updates the active type-3 record in place for consecutive movement samples, widening its min/max x/y bounds and replacing the latest timestamp rather than allocating one record per move.

QueuedInputBuffer's drain method copies every record field into caller-provided QueuedInputEvent instances before advancing the ring head, proving this is the immutable-by-consumption queue record shape.
Client interprets the record type as reset/control/press/release/movement during processQueuedMouseInput, so the record is broader than a raw java.awt.event.MouseEvent.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for one queued client-input record, including coalesced mouse movement and ordered switch/control events.
